days.note: WTA lists Longs Pass at 2.9 mi and about 2,100 ft from the Esmeralda trailhead. From the pass, drop roughly 1,400 ft to camp on Ingalls Creek; Mountain Project notes good camping there but warns of mice. There is no water between the trailhead and the creek. days.note: From the Ingalls Creek trail, go up the first major clearing west of Ulrich's Couloir into the West Ridge couloir. Take the right fork near 7,000 ft beneath black slabs to the cirque near 8,700 ft. The 4-5 pitches are mostly 4th and low 5th, with two short 5.7 sections and a ledge belay on every pitch (Mountain Project). Several thousand feet of loose scree make this a long day. The usual south-side descent is the Cascadian Couloir back to the creek; climberkyle describes it as about 4,500 ft from the creek to the summit.

sectionBreakdown.note: From the North Fork Quinault trailhead at road's end, the trail follows the valley floor through old-growth forest past Wolf Bar and Halfway House. sectionBreakdown.note: Ford the North Fork at Sixteen Mile (normally knee- to thigh-deep and swift, and hazardous or impassable in heavy rain or snowmelt), then make the steep, loose climb to Low Divide (3,602 ft), the pass between the Quinault and Elwha drainages. Continue into Seattle Creek Basin and up to a meadow camp near 4,550 ft at Seattle Meadows, below the peak's west slopes.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Over the Sixteen Mile ford to Low Divide and high camp

sectionBreakdown.note: Leave the tent at camp and go light. Ascend talus on the peak's eastern side to gain the upper south/east ridge, then Class 2-3 scree and scrambling to the 6,246 ft summit; reverse the same line back to camp.
Drop back to Low Divide, descend the steep trail to the Sixteen Mile ford and continue down the North Fork valley as far as is reasonable with a full pack after a summit day.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Back down to the North Fork

sectionBreakdown.note: Finish down the North Fork Quinault valley to the cars, re-crossing the Elip Creek and Wild Rose Creek fords. A long but easy-grade final day.

itinerary.cal: July through October; a walk-up North Cascades National Park cross-country permit from Marblemount is required. Snow conditions in the col gully change the character of the route through the season.

days.note: Take the Goodell Creek roadbed about 4 miles to the Terror Creek turnoff, climb the steep Barrier path to timberline, and traverse Stump Hollow to the saddle near 6,400 ft. Good bivies sit below Terror in Crescent Creek Basin, with a decent one just below the Himmel-Otto col. Many parties take two days for this approach.
days.title: Goodell Creek over the Barrier
days.objective: Reach a camp above Crescent Creek Basin

days.note: Climb the narrow gully to the Himmel-Otto col. Early in the season it is all snow with a little scrambling near the top; late in the season expect icy snow, chossy moats, and a loose class 3-4 bypass of an overhanging boulder. Four pitches of 5.7 PG13 lead to the summit. Descend by scrambling early season, or rappel through the moats late season.
days.title: Gully to the col and Wild Hair Crack
days.objective: Climb to the Himmelhorn summit and return to camp

days.note: Reverse Stump Hollow and the Barrier, cross Terror Creek near 2,000 ft, and follow the roadbed back. Abegg's party took about 7 hours from the Chopping Block camp.
days.title: Walk out to Goodell Creek
days.objective: Return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Three days: approach over the Barrier into the Crescent Creek side, climb the gully to the Himmel-Otto col and four pitches to the summit, then walk out in about 7 hours.

days.note: Water taxi to Big Beaver Landing, then the Big Beaver Trail and a bushwhack up Access Creek to a base camp below Access Col. Heavy packs with rock rack, ropes, and 5-6 days of food.
days.title: Boat + hike to Access Basin

schedule.label: Water taxi to Big Beaver Landing

days.objective: Reach camp at Access Basin (~4,300 ft)

days.note: Climb Access Col and traverse to Luna Pass, then continue up East Fury's Southeast Glacier to a bivy near its summit — the jumping-off point for the ridge traverse to West Fury. This is the hardest approach day: steep scree, heather, and glacier travel back to back.
days.title: Over Access Col and up East Fury to a ridge-start camp
days.objective: Camp high on/near East Fury, poised to drop onto Mongo Ridge

days.note: Descend from East Fury into the upper Goodell Creek basin to the toe of the ridge and begin working through the first of the route's gendarmes, mixing 5th-class pitches with rappels. Slow, technical ground — a fraction of a mile of actual progress for a full day's effort. Bivy on the ridge.
days.title: Onto Mongo Ridge — first gendarmes
days.objective: Descend from East Fury to the toe of the ridge and start the technical climb

days.note: More of the same: pitches up to 5.10/5.11, exposed scrambling between towers, and rappels off loose rock in one of the most remote sections of the lower 48. Rockfall is a real hazard on rappels here. Bivy again on the ridge.
days.title: Deeper into the ridge — the Pole of Remoteness
days.objective: Continue past the ridge's most remote, hardest pitches

days.note: A final ~500 ft of class 4 terrain gains West Fury's summit, typically reached by mid-morning. From there it's hours of connecting-ridge scrambling back past East Fury toward a camp at Luna Col.

schedule.detail: long ridge scrambling

days.objective: Finish the ridge to West Fury's summit, then retreat toward Luna Col

days.note: Reverse the full approach from Luna Col down through Access Basin and out the Big Beaver Trail to the landing for the water taxi — a long final day after five hard ones.
